assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral constraints propagate shocks and link finance to aggregate fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the central collateral mechanism, while Gertler is a leading architect of the financial-accelerator framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has shaped macroeconomic research and policy analysis over several decades.
uncertainties: The candidate package encompasses related mechanisms with several important contributors.
The appropriate boundary between foundational theory and later quantitative implementations is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made resource misallocation a central, quantitatively operational explanation for large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow provided an influential empirical-quantitative framework, with Restuccia making major complementary contributions to the broader misallocation literature.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are well established and have generated extensive work across countries, sectors, and policy questions.
uncertainties: Measured distortions need not map cleanly to underlying policy or institutional causes.
Credit allocation across a broad literature remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and empirical analysis of trade gains and adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical heterogeneous-firm mechanism; Helpman and Redding made major linked theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in trade research and has accumulated substantial empirical support.
uncertainties: The field contains many related contributors, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research clarified how technology, tasks, and trade shocks reshape labour demand, local adjustment, and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are strongly associated with the most influential task and trade-shock evidence.
assessment.maturity: The findings have had enduring influence across labour, trade, and public-policy research.
uncertainties: The candidate combines distinct technology and trade literatures.
The causal magnitude and persistence of adjustment effects remain active research questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially changed the analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission through households.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are closely identified with the influential HANK framework and its quantitative implications.
assessment.maturity: The agenda is highly influential and increasingly integrated into policy-oriented macroeconomics.
uncertainties: Its comparatively recent development leaves less time for long-run assessment.
Empirical discrimination among alternative household and market structures remains incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme established management practices and organisational capital as measurable determinants of firm productivity and aggregate performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen developed the core measurement and research agenda, with Sadun a major contributor to its extension and institutional relevance.
assessment.maturity: It has produced a large body of cross-country evidence and stimulated work on managerial interventions.
uncertainties: Separating causal management effects from selection and complementary institutions remains challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied central intertemporal tools for open-economy macroeconomics and framed enduring exchange-rate puzzles.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the clear principal figures in the modern intertemporal open-economy framework.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is long-standing, widely taught, and foundational for international macroeconomics.
uncertainties: The exchange-rate disconnect remains unresolved, complicating assessment of the framework's empirical closure.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research made uncertainty and policy uncertainty empirically tractable and connected them to firm decisions and macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Bloom developed the uncertainty-shock agenda, while Baker and Davis were central to the policy-uncertainty measurement programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has become influential in macroeconomic measurement and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Measures of uncertainty may partly reflect contemporaneous economic conditions rather than exogenous shocks.
The causal size of uncertainty effects remains debated.
